messages:
ana (product): Ok team — Q3 roadmap callout: we need a concrete embeddings API spec to ship a v1 that balances cost and accuracy. Can we list constraints + must-haves?

matt (eng-platform): +1. Main platform constraints: GPU memory and inference concurrency will shape max batch size. For current infra (A10G pools) practical max batch is ~1024 vectors of 1536 dims before OOM unless we shard. p99 latency target for hosted: 150ms for single-vector requests, 400ms for batch up to 128.

liam (eng-ml): customers asking for 512, 1536, and a few experimental 2048 dims. Models we can realistically support for launch: rw-embed-small-512, rw-embed-base-1536. 2048 would need new model + infra changes. Recommendation: launch with 512 and 1536 dims.

sara (solutions): Customer signals: Vector DB partners want a stable response shape and predictable per-vector cost. Enterprise customers want deterministic float32 vs quantized int8 options for on-prem. Also requests for chunked responses when input > limit.

ana (product): @liam do we have evals comparing retrieval quality 512 vs 1536 on our benchmark? Need pass/fail for launch criteria.

liam (eng-ml): Quick numbers: on our semantic-search bench, 1536 improves recall@10 by ~6 pts vs 512. Latency cost per vector ~1.9x. I'll add the exact eval CSV to the PR but baseline for launch: 1536 must be >4pt improvement vs 512 to justify higher cost.

matt (eng-platform): API surface decisions: single endpoint /v1/embeddings that accepts array of inputs and optional params: {"model","dimension_hint","stream":false,"compress":false}. We need to decide: return embeddings as array of floats or provide a compressed base64 payload option to reduce bandwidth. Thoughts?

sara (solutions): compressed base64 option would help mobile customers. But keep default as float arrays for simplicity and SDK ergonomics. Also provide per-item metadata in response: input_index, warnings.

olga (security): For on-prem and VPC, ensure we support returning embeddings without retaining inputs in logs. Add explicit header X-privacy-keep: true for retention controls. Also call out that embedding vectors are considered derived data and need same export controls.

ana (product): Launch must-haves I propose: 1) Support for batch up to 128 vectors in one call (server-side batching up to 1024 internal) 2) dims: 512 + 1536 3) Response default: float32 arrays; optional compressed base64 param 4) SDK helpers (node/python) that stream results and backoff on 429s 5) Perf SLOs: single-vector p99 < 150ms, batch128 p95 < 400ms 6) Eval pass: 1536 >= +4pt recall@10 vs 512 7) Migration guide + sample scripts.

matt (eng-platform): Implementation notes: server supports internal continuous batching; we'll expose a config `max_client_batch=128`. If customer set bigger, we will error 413. For compressed payloads we'll accept `compression: "zstd+base64"`. Suggest default compression disabled.

liam (eng-ml): Model selection: map model names to dims in catalog. Example: rw-embed-small-512 -> dims=512 cost=0.0003/vector; rw-embed-base-1536 -> dims=1536 cost=0.0007/vector. We'll finalize pricing soon. Also add explicit `model_family` tag to help routing to cheaper variants.

ana (product): What about streaming embeddings? Any benefit?

matt (eng-platform): Streaming vectors not useful — embeddings are generated from a complete input. Streaming only applicable for very large docs when we chunk; better to return chunked array.

sara (solutions): A couple of customers want a stable UUID per input text across model versions. We should document that embeddings are not stable across model changes. Recommend we offer a signed hash helper in SDKs but mark as advisory.

olga (security): Also recommend explicit opt-in flag `store_embeddings=false` for Hosted so we can guarantee not stored for enterprise.

ana (product): Ok next — owner/plan. Action items: 
- liam: finalize eval CSV + confirm cost ratio (due 1794510800)
- matt: API contract PR with example responses + error codes + compression scheme (due 1794511200)
- sara: collect top 5 customer asks and use-cases for migration guide (due 1794512000)
- olga: privacy opt-in header wording and security checklist (due 1794511600)

matt (eng-platform): I'll start the API PR. Quick example response we plan to document:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
body: {"model":"rw-embed-base-1536","inputs":["a","b"],"compression":false}
response: {"data":[{"input_index":0,"embedding":[0.001, -0.23, ...]}, {"input_index":1,"embedding":[...] }], "model":"rw-embed-base-1536"}
```

liam (eng-ml): +1 on response shape. Add `model_version` and `dimensions` fields on top-level response.

ana (product): Great. If no blockers we'll add this to the roadmap doc and sync on Monday to finalize scope. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled infra window 1794513600-1794517200 for model catalog rollout (no user impact expected).
